memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah, "When you are helping the Hebrew women during childbirth on the delivery stool, if you see that the baby is a boy, kill him; but if it is a girl, let her live." The midwives, however, feared God and did not do what the king of Egypt had told them to do; they let the boys live." - Exodus 1:15-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh is the most powerful man on earth, and the Bible does not even record his name. But it carefully records theirs: Shiphrah and Puah. Two midwives. That tells you whose side heaven is on.

They were given a direct order from an absolute ruler, backed by the power of life and death. And they quietly refused. Not with speeches or protests — they simply kept delivering babies and letting them live.

The reason is given plainly: they feared God. The fear of God is not terror; it is taking God more seriously than anyone else. When you fear God most, you can face lesser powers without panic.

There are moments when obedience to God will cost us at work, in college, in a family under pressure to compromise. The apostles put it simply: we must obey God rather than men (Acts 5:29). That line has been the courage of believers ever since.

You may never lead a nation. But like these women, you can quietly refuse to do what is wrong today — and heaven will remember your name.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I being pressured to do something I know is wrong?
2. Whom do I fear more — God, or the people who can affect my future?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me the quiet courage of Shiphrah and Puah. May I fear You more than I fear any person or consequence. Amen.
